applicant_utility.summary: This is a host-organisation-anchored fellowship: your New Zealand host must be registered in the Royal Society's portal before the application can be lodged, so the conversation with your prospective host matters more than any document. The window is tight and annual - the 2026 round ran from 1 May to 2.00pm on 9 July - so watch the Royal Society's funds page rather than generic scholarship aggregators for the next round.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Early-career researchers within four years of PhD conferral who have a New Zealand host research organisation willing to register them in the portal.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are within 0-4 years of research experience since PhD conferral
Secure a New Zealand host research organisation and have it registered in the online portal
Prepare the application for the narrow annual window (2026: 1 May to 9 July, 2.00pm NZST close)
Draft the four-year research plan around the NZ$820,000 fellowship value
common_rejection_risks: Being more than four years past PhD conferral
A host that is not a New Zealand research organisation registered in the portal
Missing the 2.00pm cut-off on the closing date
Submitting without a host relationship in place, which the scheme's structure requires
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Not published on the fellowship page; check the scheme's terms before budgeting beyond the fellowship value.
document_audit: The application runs through the Royal Society portal with the host registered in the same system
The published fellowship value covers a four-year term, so annual budgeting should follow that scale
alerts: The next round's opening and closing dates are not published yet - the Society announces them on this page
The scheme sits within the wider Tawhia te Mana Research Fellowships, whose other schemes have different eligibility
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register with a New Zealand host organisation in the Royal Society portal, then apply during the annual window.

official.deadline_note: Applications to support study in 2027 closed on Sunday 19 July 2026, with outcomes notified by late November 2026. Applications to support study in 2028 will open mid-2027; no exact 2028 closing date is published.
official.application_cycle: Annual; 2027-study round closed 19 July 2026, 2028-study round opens mid-2027
official.status_note: The Ministry states applications to support study in 2028 will open mid-2027; the 2027 round closed 19 July 2026.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Awards are cash scholarships valued per level: $10,000 VET, up to $30,000 undergraduate, up to $20,000 master's, up to $20,000 Master of Education research, up to $40,000 doctoral.
official.funding_amount_note: 14 scholarships each year: 5 VET at $10,000 (minimum 120 credits, NZQA level 4-7 non-degree), 4 undergraduate up to $30,000 ($10,000 per year for up to 3 years), 3 master's up to $20,000 ($10,000 per year for up to 2 years), 1 Master of Education research up to $20,000, and 1 doctoral up to $40,000 ($20,000 per year for up to 2 years).
benefits: 5 VET scholarships valued at $10,000 for study of at least 120 credits at NZQA level 4-7 (non-degree)
4 undergraduate scholarships valued up to $30,000 ($10,000 per year for up to 3 years)
3 master's scholarships valued up to $20,000 ($10,000 per year for up to 2 years)
1 Master of Education research scholarship valued up to $20,000
1 doctoral scholarship valued up to $40,000 ($20,000 per year for up to 2 years)
Fund increased by $100,000 per year from the 2026-2027 Budget, adding 5 scholarships to reach 14 annually
eligibility: Of Maori descent or whakapapa to a recognised Maori iwi
Enrolling in, or already enrolled to continue, full-time tertiary study for the 2027 academic year
Preference is given to applicants whose studies aim to improve the social, economic and cultural wellbeing of Maori
requirements: VET applicants: course leading to a certificate or diploma at NZQA level 4-7, at least 120 credits, studied full time
Master's applicants: verified tertiary transcript, endorsement, and a statement of up to 250 words outlining the topic and interest
Doctoral applicants: a 500-word essay on the thesis topic and future expectations, plus a chief supervisor reference confirming acceptance
documents: Record of achievement or other record of learning (VET): MyBCITO record, tertiary transcript, NZQA record for NCEA, or provider record
Verified tertiary academic transcript (undergraduate and master's) or NZQA record of learning for NCEA Level 2 (and 3 if applicable)
Reference or endorsement commenting on achievement and suitability, from a lecturer, tutor, teacher, workplace assessor or community leader - not from a friend or family member
250-word statement (master's) or 500-word essay plus supervisor reference (doctoral)
selection_criteria: Values aligned with those of the 28th Maori Battalion
Preference for studies that improve the social, economic and cultural wellbeing of Maori
Fund board awards to exceptional Maori students for vocational or tertiary study
coverage: Cash scholarships toward tertiary or vocational study; living and travel costs are not covered
application_method: Apply online when the round opens (the 2027 round is closed)
official.application_route: Online application form published by the Ministry of Education, awarded by the Ngarimu VC and 28th (Maori) Battalion Memorial Scholarship Fund Board
official.citizenship_residency: Maori descent or whakapapa to a recognised Maori iwi
official.international_eligibility: Domestic scheme for Maori students; no international eligibility
official.duration: One year, renewing up to 3 years (undergraduate) or 2 years (master's and doctoral)
official.description: The Ngarimu VC and 28th (Maori) Battalion Memorial Scholarships are annual awards funded by the Ngarimu VC and 28th (Maori) Battalion Memorial Scholarship Fund Board, established by the 1945 Act, for Maori students demonstrating values aligned with the 28th Maori Battalion.

verification.notes: All award values, the 19 July 2026 close and the document requirements were read live from the Ministry of Education page (last updated 30 July 2026) on 2026-10-11.

applicant_utility.summary: The reference letter is the piece applicants underestimate: it must come from someone in your study or training journey and cannot be a friend or family member, so ask your lecturer or workplace assessor early. Apply in the year before the study year - the 2027-study round closed 19 July 2026 and paid out during 2027 - so the correct window is roughly a year ahead of your enrolment.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Maori students of full-time tertiary age in vocational, undergraduate, master's or doctoral study whose work improves Maori social, economic and cultural wellbeing.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm whakapapa to a recognised Maori iwi and full-time enrolment status
Request the reference or endorsement from a lecturer, tutor, teacher or workplace assessor (never a friend or family member)
Assemble the record of achievement: verified transcript or NZQA record of learning
Draft the word-limited statement early: 250 words at master's, 500 words at doctoral
Watch for the 2028-study round opening mid-2027
common_rejection_risks: A reference from a friend or family member, which is explicitly not accepted
Part-time study, which falls outside the award
Missing the July close of the round preceding your study year
A statement over the word limit or off-topic
For doctoral applicants, lacking the chief supervisor reference confirming PhD acceptance
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs, travel and any study expenses beyond the awarded value.
document_audit: VET applicants can use a MyBCITO record or provider record instead of a formal transcript
An apprenticeship does not forfeit the award if you change employer but stay enrolled
Master's applicants need both a transcript and an endorsement plus the 250-word statement
alerts: The fund grew by $100,000 a year from the 2026-2027 Budget, lifting the total to 14 scholarships each year - a slightly better field than in previous years
Preference goes to studies improving Maori wellbeing, so frame the statement around contribution, not only personal achievement
The 2026-2027 application guidelines PDF on the page is the best guide to formats while the round is closed
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply online in the round that precedes your study year (July close), with documents and references attached; outcomes arrive the following November.
